name: Paravilhana
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1, languoid para1309 'Paravilhana' (refs: Meira 2006; Howard 2001; Gildea 2012; d'Almada 1861; Martius 1867; Adam 1893).
sources.note: No descriptive reference listed; all six refs are subclassification comments or historical mentions.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1928. Vom Roroima zum Orinoco, Band IV: Sprachen. Stuttgart: Strecker und Schröder.
sources.note: Contains no Paravilhana material at all (zero hits for 'paravil' in the full scanned text); its Rio Branco Cariban lists are Sapará, Purukotó, Wayumará, Pauxiana.

sources.citation: Adam, Lucien. 1893. Matériaux pour servir à l'établissement d'une grammaire comparée des dialectes de la famille caribe. Bibliothèque linguistique américaine XVII. Paris: Maisonneuve.
sources.note: Nothing on stress for any language; the 'Accidents phonétiques' chapter treats aphaeresis/syncope/apocope. Paravilhana appears only in the source list ('Paravilhanas. Haut Rio Branco et Guyane anglaise. Natterer, 1832. Vocab. inséré dans l'ouvrage de Martius') and in possessive-prefix notes (e.g. 'Paravilhana. — Indices : r-, l-. Ex. : r-ampu-liu (son) doigt').

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, II: Zur Sprachenkunde (Wörtersammlung brasilianischer Sprachen / Glossaria linguarum Brasiliensium). Leipzig: Fleischer. Paravilhana wordlist pp. 227-228, 'Von Natterer im Forte do Rio Branco am 26. Jan. 1832 aufgezeichnet'.
sources.note: Nothing. A ~200-item Latin-glossed wordlist only; many forms carry an acute accent (dóna 'aqua', ulapá/urapá 'arcus', vokulú 'bibam', amanpé 'celer', kó palé 'cras', lampulú 'manus'), mostly on the final syllable, but no note in the volume explains the accents for this list (Martius's general remark on p. 29 that the accent ' 'dient, den Vocal zu schärfen oder die Sylbe zu betonen' is made in the Tupi section).

sources.citation: Lobo d'Almada, Manoel da Gama. 1861 [1787]. Descripção relativa ao Rio Branco e seu território. Revista Trimensal do Instituto Historico, Geographico e Ethnographico do Brasil 24 (4.º trimestre): 617-683.
sources.note: Nothing; ethnographic notice only (p. 674: 'Os paravilhanos, que habitam hoje para as cabeceiras do rio Tacutú..'), no language data.
Nothing on phonology; says the language is extinct and poorly attested (last speaker d. 1914 per en.wikipedia), classification Venezuelan Cariban / Mapoyo-Tamanaku group with Pauxiana and Sapará.

sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F.H. & Hélène B. Brijnen. 2014. Johann Natterer and the Amazonian languages. Revista Brasileira de Linguística Antropológica 6(2): 333-352.

tone.quote: In the Bororo language samples, which were among the first to be elaborated by Natterer, he made ample use of diacritic signs, most of which are difficult to interpret today. [...] In some cases, the meaning of a diacritic is obvious, also because Natterer adds a comment to such effect. For instance, in the Bororo word ito̅narageté ‘[my] daughter’, recorded in Natterer’s lists, the acute accent of the symbol é serves to indicate that the vowel represented is not a front vowel [e], but rather a central vowel [ï] (stummes e).
tone.locator: pp. 339-340; Cabixí tonal remark p. 338; Paravilhana mentions pp. 335, 337

sources.citation: Goeje, C. H. de. 1909. Études linguistiques caraïbes. (Verhandelingen der Koninklijke Akademie van Wetenschappen te Amsterdam, Afdeeling Letterkunde, Nieuwe Reeks, Deel X, No. 3.) Amsterdam: Johannes Müller. [archive.org item;gov.ignca.32223 is the whole of N.R. Deel X (volume dated 1910), in which this is no. 3]

tone.quote: Il n'est pas facile de trouver des règles pour l'accent dans les dialectes caraibes, le matériel étant trop limité; st [=si] nous en donnons une, c'est sous la plus grande réserve, Règle: l'accent principal d'un mot tombe sur la penultieme de la racine
tone.locator: §19 'Accent' of the comparative grammar, p. 84-85 (running head '85 ÉTUDES LINGUISTIQUES CARAÏBES' follows the passage)
tone.translation: It is not easy to find rules for the accent in the Carib dialects, the material being too limited; if we give one, it is with the greatest reservation. Rule: the main accent of a word falls on the penultimate syllable of the root.
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)

tone.says: Viewed: c. 165-entry German-prompted wordlist; many forms carry acute (occasionally grave/macron) marks, e.g. nopussá, vischiká, lampulú, karapelí, dóná ~ duná; the leaves seen carry no note explaining the diacritics, so the sole primary record gives no statement on stress or tone — the marks are the only prosodic evidence that will ever exist for para1309.
